headline: LIGHTS OUT: Meridian 88 Goes Dark for Eight Brutal Days
body:
Meridian 88 fell into total darkness at 11:47 PM on March 14th when a cascading failure ripped through the Ferrogate Transit power grid, taking the city's primary, secondary, and tertiary distribution networks offline within six minutes. All eight districts lost power simultaneously — the first total blackout in the megacity's recorded history. Emergency lighting in The Spires held for approximately forty minutes before those reserves were drained by competing corporate systems fighting to protect their own server infrastructure.

Within the first 24 hours, The Shelf and The Narrows descended into open chaos. Without power, NovaMind BCI implants operating on city-relay bandwidth began throwing error cascades — doctors report over 1,400 people hospitalized citywide for neurological symptoms related to signal dropout. Bore Rats emerged from The Underworld in organized waves, and sources on the ground say they effectively controlled Old Harbor's food distribution within 48 hours.

Ferrogate Transit issued a statement on day three blaming a simultaneous failure of three relay substations in Geartown, calling it a 'statistically impossible coincidence.' The Lake Monitor has since obtained internal diagnostic logs suggesting the failure was not coincidental — the substations were deliberately overloaded via a remote intrusion. The Federal Remnant deployed 2,000 emergency personnel on day four, but their jurisdiction was disputed immediately by Axiom and Ironclad representatives.

Power was fully restored on March 22nd, eight days after the initial failure. The official death toll stands at 312, a number that independent analysts and the Shelf Voice dispute sharply, placing the real count above 900 when accounting for medical equipment failures, violence, and exposure deaths in The Narrows.
aftermath: Ferrogate Transit was placed under an emergency oversight council controlled jointly by Axiom and Ironclad, a power arrangement that has yet to be dissolved as of this reporting.
runner_relevance: The Blackout created one of the most active runner markets in a decade. Immediate contracts included emergency courier runs replacing dead BCI-network messaging, medical supply smuggling from stockpiles in The Circuit to hospitals in The Narrows, and protection details for anyone with a working generator. After power was restored, the real money arrived: data retrieval contracts from corporations desperate to recover the eight days of lost surveillance footage, and investigative work tracing the source of the substation intrusion — at least four competing clients wanted that information, and all of them were willing to pay above 50,000 phi for it.
